incumbent.name: Wendy Dant Chesser
incumbent.summary: Wendy Dant Chesser of Jeffersonville, a former president and CEO of One Southern Indiana, was sworn in on June 4, 2024 after local Democrats chose her to finish Rep. Rita Fleming's term {caucus_dc} {lpm_2024_hd71}. She won a full term in November 2024 {lpm_2024_result} and is seeking a second {lpm_filed}.
record: Committees: Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; Financial Institutions; Insurance; and Roads and Transportation {caucus_dc}.

2025: Authored HEA 1226, the "Birthday Rule," which lets Medicare supplement (Medigap) enrollees switch plans without medical underwriting within 60 days of their birthday; it passed the House unanimously and the Senate 45-2 {caucus_dc_news} {caucus_hea1226}. Supported HB 1208, requiring quarterly reporting and training for sheriffs' jail commissary funds; in testimony she cited theft by former Clark County Sheriff Jamey Noel {caucus_dc_news}.

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) {rc_sea1_433}, and on the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) {rc_hb1001_576}; voted no on HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) {rc_hb1032_28}. Before that vote she said the proposed map was "completely unfair to residents of Southern Indiana" because it joined Jeffersonville with west-side Indianapolis {caucus_dc_news2}.

Voted no on HB 1461 (2025), which allows new tolls on Indiana roads, saying "We cannot have more tolling in Southern Indiana" {caucus_dc_news}. Voted no on HB 1343 (2026), citing a provision on a National Guard military police force the governor could deploy without local consent {caucus_dc_news2}.

2026 bills she filed included a state-employer-parent child-care cost-sharing program, a pooled-benefits plan for child-care providers, a 3,520-foot buffer between vape or smoke shops and schools, and a first-time homebuyer savings program {caucus_dc_news2}.

race_context: House District 71 covers Jeffersonville, Clarksville and part of New Albany, in Clark and Floyd counties {lpm_2024_result} {caucus_dc}.

Not an open seat: Dant Chesser is the incumbent. She was chosen by a Democratic caucus in May 2024 after Rep. Rita Fleming retired immediately after the 2024 primary {lpm_2024_hd71b}. In November 2024 she defeated Republican Scott Hawkins and Libertarian Greg Hertzsch; in Clark County she received 49.4% to Hawkins' 46.7% {lpm_2024_result}.
May 5, 2026 Republican primary: James McClure Jr. 1,337 votes (55.1%), D.M. Bagshaw 1,090 (44.9%) {wiki_2026}. Dant Chesser was unopposed in the Democratic primary {lpm_primary_list} {wiki_2026}.
A Floyd County Republican Party debate before the primary included the Republican House District 71 candidates {lpm_hd72_debate}. No general-election debate or forum for this race was found.

Key differences: Dant Chesser's campaign emphasizes jobs, child care, workforce training and government accountability {dc_site}; in 2024 McClure listed repealing "red flag" laws, shrinking state government and parents' rights as priorities {lpm_2024_primary_guide}.

candidates.summary: James McClure Jr. is an Air Force and Navy veteran who has worked in information technology {lpm_2024_primary_guide}. He lost the 2024 Republican primary for this seat and won the 2026 primary with 55.1% {lpm_2024_primary} {wiki_2026}.
background: In a 2024 LPM questionnaire he described himself as a veteran of the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Navy, including a 2005 deployment to Iraq, with 30 years in IT and more than 20 years of citizen activism {lpm_2024_primary_guide}.

Lists an associate degree from the Community College of the Air Force (1990), four years in the Air Force and five in the Navy Reserve, and Knights of Columbus membership {ivg_mcclure}. Has previously sought a U.S. House seat {ivg_mcclure}.
path_to_ballot: Lost the 2024 Republican primary for District 71 to Scott Hawkins, 3,199 votes to 880 {lpm_2024_primary}.
Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over D.M. Bagshaw, 1,337 votes (55.1%) to 1,090 {wiki_2026}.

items: In 2024 listed eliminating "red flag" laws and other state laws he considers unconstitutional as a priority {lpm_2024_primary_guide}.
In 2024 called for reducing the size and scope of state government by eliminating waste and redundancy to ease the tax burden {lpm_2024_primary_guide}.
In 2024 said he would protect parents' right to raise and educate their children as they see fit {lpm_2024_primary_guide}.

on_incumbent: No 2026 statements by McClure about Dant Chesser or her record were found.
plans: In 2024 said he would work with the next governor to "nullify federal overreach" and promised to serve a full term if elected {lpm_2024_primary_guide}.
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement he reported from state Sen. Chris Garten {ivg_mcclure}. In 2024 he said he had accepted only local donations {lpm_2024_primary_guide}. No 2026 fundraising totals were verified.
gaps: His positions above come from a 2024 questionnaire; no 2026 questionnaire answers, campaign website or news interviews were found.

Unverified (search snippets only): an Indiana Capital Chronicle voter guide says he previously ran in Democratic primaries for the 9th Congressional District in 2010, 2014 and 2016; lists his employer as Booth Veneer; and says his 2026 primary priorities were property taxes, eliminating fraud in state government and protecting liberty. iVoterGuide also lists a 2014 contribution from him to a Democratic Party organization.
What he said at the Floyd County Republican debate was not reported in the sources found.

candidates.summary: Wendy Dant Chesser is the incumbent, in office since June 2024 {caucus_dc}. She led One Southern Indiana, the Clark-Floyd economic development group and chamber, for more than a decade {caucus_dc}.
background: Jeffersonville native; graduated from Jeffersonville High School and IU Southeast (business management); certified economic developer {caucus_dc} {dc_site}.

Worked in the O'Bannon/Kernan administration and led the Indiana Rural Development Council; president and CEO of One Southern Indiana from 2012 {dc_site} {caucus_dc}. As of 2024 she was chief director of corporate strategy and external affairs at a regional employer {lpm_2024_hd71b}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {lpm_primary_list} {wiki_2026}.

items: Authored the 2025 Medigap "Birthday Rule" law, saying it lowers seniors' risk of being denied coverage because of past claims or pre-existing conditions {caucus_hea1226}.

Says Indiana ranks 50th in licensed child-care facilities per capita and supports grants, tax credits and support for providers and parents {dc_site}; filed 2026 bills to share child-care costs among the state, employers and parents {caucus_dc_news2}.
Filed 2025 bills requiring ethics training for local elected officials and changing local campaign-finance reporting, and backed tighter jail commissary fund reporting {caucus_dc_news}.
Opposed allowing more tolling, saying people cross the Ohio River bridges often to work or go to school {caucus_dc_news}.
Opposed the 2025 congressional map, saying Southern Indiana is "impacted more by Louisville than by Indianapolis" {caucus_dc_news2}; voted no on HB 1032 {rc_hb1032_28}.
Her campaign says she will keep fighting for the region's share of the state budget and for higher-paying jobs {dc_site}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Dant Chesser about McClure were found.
plans: Campaign priorities: transparency and accountability, jobs, education and workforce development, and affordable child care {dc_site}.
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists endorsements from the AFL-CIO, the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, Better Indiana, Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and the Indiana House Democratic Caucus {ivg_dc}. No 2026 fundraising totals were verified.
gaps: No public statement by her on the Meta data center being built in Jeffersonville was found.
Her yes votes on SEA 1 and the 2025 budget are from roll calls; no statements explaining those votes were found.
No campaign finance reports were reviewed.
